newsitem.title: USA: Workers strike GM truck plant in Ohio.
newsitem.headline: Workers strike GM truck plant in Ohio.

text.p: About 4,100 unionized workers at General Motors Corp.'s truck plant in Moraine, Ohio, went on strike early Sunday morning, a day after they voted down a new local contract with the automaker.
Members of the International Union of Electronics Workers (IUE) walked off the job shortly after midnight Sunday and pickets continued throughout the day at the plant near Dayton, Ohio.

Production of Chevrolet Blazer and GMC Jimmy compact sport/utility, normally scheduled to resume at about 5 a.m. EST Monday, was expected to remain idle unless the dispute is resolved. The plant operates with three production crews that keep the assembly line running about 20 hours a day, six days a week.
GM also produces the popular four-wheel-drive trucks in Linden, N.J., which is represented by the United Auto Workers union.
GM spokesman Jeff Kuhlman said no formal negotiations between the company and the union had taken place by midafternoon Sunday.
"We have not had any official contact with the union since they walked out last night," Kuhlman said.
He also said GM considered the strike illegal and was considering its options, which included seeking a court injunction to stop it.
GM reached a tentative agreement with the IUE for a new local contract at the plant last week, which came before the expiration of a five-day strike deadline the union had set.

But in voting that ended at midnight Friday, IUE workers at the plant voted against the proposed contract by a bloc of 56 percent. Officials familiar with the pact said workers were unhappy with a strict attendance policy that imposed harsh penalties on workers for absences.
GM in recent weeks also has put pressure on other IUE-represented plants in the Dayton area to cut costs to help the automaker's parts operation become competitive.
